related_work: We also worked in groups to read *Race After Technology* by Ruha Benjamin. My group focused on Default Discrimination. We discussed how technology can treat certain groups unfairly, even when discrimination is not the intention. For example, predictive policing software may use historical data that reflects existing biases, leading to more police being sent to Black communities.
results_discussion: Through reading, I learned that the problem is not simply that algorithms sometimes make mistakes. They can also reproduce existing social inequalities while making their decisions appear objective.This made me think more carefully about the technologies and data I might use in my own projects. In the future, I want to consider not only how technology works, but also whether it might unintentionally exclude or disadvantage certain people.
title: creative industry research - week 5
introduction: This week, we continued working on our Practice Grids. Miha explained the difference between values and principles. Values are what we believe in and care about, while principles are the actions we take to put those values into practice. This helped me think more clearly about what is important in my creative practice and how I can apply these ideas to my projects.
